maya: heads-up — regression seen on main after kernel-selector tweak. p90 latency up ~18% on long sequences.
alex: repro confirmed on dev; interestingly nvprof traces pre-change show continuous kernels, post-change shows tiny idle gaps between matmul kernels.
jing: do we have nsys traces for both commits? can we compare kernel timelines?
maya: yes attached two traces (links). i ran:
```
nsys profile --output before --trace=cuda,osrt --sample=none --duration=60 --capture-range=cpu:start,end ./runner --seq_len=1024 --qps=40
nsys profile --output after  --trace=cuda,osrt --sample=none --duration=60 --capture-range=cpu:start,end ./runner --seq_len=1024 --qps=40
```
alex: note i used --sample=none to get full timeline; sampling misses the sub-ms gaps.
sam: looked at flamegraphs: there is a ~200-400us gap per token between GEMM launches, that accumulates. KV cache misses spike too — eviction churn increased around the same time.
maya: i ran a quick git bisect — culprit is commit 9f1b2c4 that adjusted batcher handoff heuristics (changed scheduler spin wait -> relax/nap).
jing: that matches: relax reduces CPU spinning so GPU submission can be delayed by scheduler wakeups. small per-token delay multiplies over long seqs.
jing: quick local test: revert the spin behavior and p95/p99 go back in line.
perf-bot: note — please add an e2e perf regression test (seq=1024 qps=40) to CI with NVTX markers.
alex: immediate plan: 1) produce minimal reproducer (single GPU, seq=1024, qps=40) 2) add NVTX ranges around batcher handoff and submission 3) try tuning nap duration / backoff 4) consider coalescing submissions to reduce kernel launch frequency.
maya: i'll open a PR with the reproducer, NVTX ranges, and a perf-run script. assigning to me + alex.
sam: also run perfetto to inspect thread wakeups/syscall wake patterns — might confirm scheduler wake latency.
maya: short-term mitigation: revert the relax change on dedicated pools if customers hit this. filing rollback draft. :thumbsup:
